info.title: RAILSHOT session-scoped product API
info.description: Anonymous cookie sessions separate dashboard records; no user accounts or login. Every remote API request is session-scoped, including requests with the existing internal operator bearer. Exact Host/Origin checks remain. CI/provider execution credentials remain server-only. Optional OpenStack connection metadata is stored separately, with encrypted write-only passwords; it is not execution configuration. One API process and one persistent SQLite database on one host; one unfinished operation across all sessions. Local contract tests are not cloud deployment evidence. OpenStack registration requires the configured operator Bearer, stores only a salted hash of the user-supplied enrollment key, and returns a 10-minute one-time linkage token. The existing install.sh is served unchanged. Personal environments use a separate persistent owner cookie and one-time-visible recovery key, without adding an external login provider; recovery rotates both capabilities.

post.description: Persist a normalized private source snapshot and execution intent before any external mutation. Without plan_id, require the app-bound target in server CD configuration or a successful saved environment registration; reuse does not provision VMs or databases again. An environment/provider selection resolves the existing registered target server-side. Optional plan_id is only accepted with explicit app/target_id and consumes an executable, unexpired, unchanged plan for the same app and runtime target; its profile must include deployment registration. Complete environment execution and registration before CI, verified publication and CD. Environment or database success alone does not mean application deployment succeeded. Deployments and updates persist in a bounded FIFO; one writer executes at a time. A finished unknown worker releases its global slot after 60 seconds. An unknown registered CD/HTTP result with verified publication fences that environment; uncertain CI/registration or missing bindings still fence the shared app source across environments. Unclaimed queued deployments survive restart; started operations never auto-replay. Same GitHub URL/key reuses the first SHA without refetching HEAD; plan_id and environment/provider selection are part of idempotent input.

post.description: Strict JSON. name is an application name of 3 through 30 characters. Operator profiles expose no credentials or local paths. Execution supports one registered AWS/GCP amd64 runtime node with database.mode=none or configured Patroni placements. Each placement must exactly match its registered database, DCS voter and proxy role counts; the combined topology needs at least two database nodes, at least three odd-numbered DCS voters and at least one proxy. standalone and unsupported runtime counts/providers/topologies produce a saved non-executable plan with blockers. Plans expire after 15 minutes, bind policy and target snapshots plus every provider plan digest, and admit only new resources without changes to existing resources. Plan creation uses the same execution admission lock. A saved or executable plan is not deployment evidence. For profiles with deployment configuration, the target database binding requirement must equal whether the request uses patroni; mismatches produce DATABASE_BINDING_PROFILE_MISMATCH before Terraform planning. Profiles without deployment configuration can independently select database preparation.

get.summary: Read CI progress and the bounded deployment timeline
get.description: The owning session and persisted deployment/run/source/app/target binding are checked before any GitHub read or cache access. Reads only the registered workflow, branch and repository, then the current attempt GitHub Actions check named Railshot agent events. The exact external ID, head SHA, details URL, producer and envelope bindings must match. No previous-attempt fallback. Strict schema rejects raw text, commands, reasoning and unknown fields. At most 60 recent items and 60,000 UTF-8 bytes; truncation is explicit. GitHub reads are bounded to five pages of twenty checks and 2 MiB per response. A process-local cache retains at most 100 source/attempt identities for 15 seconds; run identity is checked before and after reading. Complete describes observation completion, never CI success. Stale means a running observation is over 60 seconds old. Missing older producers remain not_started/not_available. No query parameters or mutation methods are accepted. The timeline field includes session-scoped dispatch/publication/config/controller/workload/HTTP observations, at most 240 events retained for seven days. It is evidence, not execution authority. The progress projection provides the last observed gate or SDK event, optional executor-declared budget capped at two, and confirmed SDK invocation count or null. Dashboard readers poll after 15 seconds and show stale after 60 seconds. Content-free SDK progress metadata is retained in the central timeline; prompts, source, commands and reasoning text remain excluded.

post.summary: Preview stopping, starting or deleting an owned application
post.description: Unknown fields, duplicate JSON keys and all query parameters are rejected. Other sessions receive 404. Operator credentials and local paths are never accepted. Registered active deployments can be deleted after cancellation/quiescence. Active deployment deletion uses a private, configuration-bound application scope and requires fresh ownership validation before cleanup. Other queued/running or unexpired unknown work blocks the shared slot; expired unknown still fences its own app or environment. Cloud inspection does not hold the product writer queue. A pending or failed plan cannot authorize any mutation. If the app changes during inspection, the plan fails as stale. Interrupted read-only planning resumes under the same public plan ID after restart with a fresh private native attempt. Application snapshot checks still apply; mutations are never replayed by recovery.

post.summary: Resume the same published application deployment
post.description: Accept only action=resume and no query parameters. Requires an exact cookie-session owner on both the deployment and ready application, status=unknown, stage=cd or http, and the original published CI evidence. Reject deletion/lifecycle intents, changed app/environment/run/source bindings and another active operation. Atomically admit one worker for this existing deployment. Recheck publication artifact ID, producer attempt and image digests before updating CI evidence. Do not register an app, submit CI, replace source, or clear native journals. Native uncertain writes remain blocked or read-only reconciled according to their existing contracts; resume does not guarantee success. Concurrent duplicate calls return 409. Idempotency-Key is not required; the existing resource ID and recorded state govern admission.

post.description: Authorize ownership, verify the current application version, freeze the submitted source and compare it with the last verified serving deployment. Retain a 30-minute preview as a deployment record. Same Idempotency-Key keeps the original snapshot, including the originally resolved GitHub SHA. No registration, source-repository write or CI dispatch.

It never substitutes the registered target app. A different app on a fixed target is rejected before source retrieval or execution; a new app needs its own registration or an executable create_per_request plan. Missing or invalid source names are rejected without a placeholder or hash fallback. Personal OpenStack selection additionally accepts target_id; multipart deployment_selection JSON is not accepted. ExecutionAdmission.description: Present on EXECUTOR_BUSY. The current action was not admitted; the scope is the shared writer, not the browser session. Blocker details are included only for its exact session owner.

OperationQueue.description: Single-replica FIFO metadata. Sequence is an admission order, not a live position. Release only drops the global slot; it never establishes an external outcome or retries the operation. Legacy unknown records can have release fields without enqueue fields.

Telemetry.description: Version 1 bounded central event journal; see docs/api/diagnostics.md.

FailureClassification.description: Durable typed hypothesis with input/rubric/model identity; never grants write or retry authority.

AgentBudget.description: Executor-declared total SDK invocation budget, up to two initial packaging calls and two repair calls. This is an allowance, not actual usage. enabled must equal max_invocations > 0. Older limits of 0, 1, 2 and 3 remain valid; missing metadata stays null.

CiProgress.description: Last observed CI progress, not execution authority. A heartbeat alone never proves an SDK invocation; actual model calls and cost cannot be inferred. Budget may be recovered only from the same run and attempt in the retained timeline.

AgentActivity.description: Read-only projection of bound host events. Agent completion does not imply repair success; repair success does not imply deployment success. No model invocation on GET.
